channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Not A Conclusion We Lose World Liberty Business: Belshe
item.description: Mike Belshe, co-founder & CEO of BitGo, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." A company tied to World Liberty Financial, the Trump family’s crypto venture, received preliminary conditional approval for a national trust bank charter from a federal regulator. It would no longer need its current issuer BitGo Bank & Trust. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Meta Announces Muse AI Agent for Personal Tasks and Organization
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. unveiled a new artificial intelligence agent designed to carry out tasks on a user’s behalf, advancing Mark Zuckerberg’s vision of a future where people each have a personalized AI assistant.
item.dc:creator: Riley Griffin

item.title: Legislative Path Required To Go Forward: Belshe
item.description: Mike Belshe, co-founder & CEO of BitGo, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They discuss the need for the passage of the Clarity Act in the US. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Truist Adds to Investment Bank With Insurance, Healthcare Hires
item.description: Cem Altuntas is joining Truist Financial Corp.’s investment bank as head of insurance brokers and services as the regional bank builds out its advisory business.
item.dc:creator: Matt Monks

item.title: AMC, Robinhood CEOs Feud Over Tokenization
item.description: Bloomberg's Anna Irrerea joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." AMC CEO Adam Aron traded barbs with Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev last week after discovering a token bearing the theater chain’s name was trading on the brokerage’s blockchain. AMC CEO dubbed it “outrageous” and demanded that Robinhood cease trading it. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Different Use Cases For Different Tokenization: Krupetsky
item.description: Morgan Krupetsky, vice president of Onchain Finance at Ava Labs, joins Scarlet Fu and Tim Stenovec on "Bloomberg Crypto." They the recent spat between AMC and Robinhood over tokenized trading and the different use cases for different tokenization models. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Amazon, Qualcomm Deal Broadens the AI Chip Race | Bloomberg Tech 9/08/2026
item.description: Bloomberg’s Riley Griffin breaks down Qualcomm's deal signing up Amazon as a data center chip customer, an agreement that will span "multiple generations." Meanwhile, another deal falls apart after Anthropic decides against acquiring AI startup Decart AI. And, all eyes are on Apple as the company kicks off its product launch tomorrow, with its foldable iPhone a decade in the making. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ramp in Talks for New Funding at $60 Billion Valuation
item.description: Ramp is in early talks with investors for a new round of funding at a roughly $60 billion valuation, according to people familiar with the efforts, just three months after the financial technology startup was valued at $44 billion. The company is considering raising about $1 billion in primary funding, said one of the people, who spoke on condition of anonymity as the information is not public. The talks are ongoing and details could change, the people said.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence and Natasha Mascarenhas

item.title: Apple Set for Major Product Launch with Foldable iPhone
item.description: Apple is gearing up for one of its biggest product launches in years, with the company expected to unveil its first foldable iPhone, a device that has been a decade in the making and which could cost as much as $2,199. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman explains how it marks the biggest design change to the iPhone in nearly twenty years. He joins Bloomberg's Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Healthcare Startup Forus Hits $3 Billion Valuation
item.description: Healthcare automation startup Forus has raised $150 million at a $3 billion valuation, tripling its value just months after its previous funding round. CEO Sahir Jaggi explains how the company uses AI agents to help patients and doctors navigate insurance coverage, affordability, and drug fulfillment. He also explains how the new capital will help Forus expand beyond autoimmune diseases into areas including oncology and neurology. He joins Bloomberg's Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Amazon Is Diversifying Its AI Chip Supply
item.description: Amazon’s expanded relationship with Qualcomm is reigniting debate over “circular financing” in the AI boom. Advisors Capital Management Partner and Portfolio Manager JoAnne Feeney discusses how the deal gives Amazon another source of custom chips and could reduce its reliance on Nvidia, while giving Qualcomm greater confidence to invest in capacity. She joins Bloomberg's Riley Griffin on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Startup Cognition Raises $2 Billion at a $48 Billion Value
item.description: Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. has raised $2 billion in a new round of funding that vaulted its valuation to $48 billion.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Oltman

item.title: Bank of America Scrambles to Refinance Internet Provider Cogent
item.description: Bank of America Corp. has discussed providing investors of Cogent Communications Holdings Inc. with additional collateral for a new money raise for the internet provider, according to people familiar with the situation.
item.dc:creator: Reshmi Basu

item.title: Canada Tariffs Escalate Trade Spat; Markets brace for Inflation Test
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Vonnie Quinn and Bailey Lipschultz on "Bloomberg Open Interest." The summer calm may be over. Middle East tensions hit markets ahead of a crucial inflation report, as the US-Canada trade fight escalates. Apple enters the John Ternus era with a foldable iPhone. Plus, NASCAR CEO Steve O’Donnell on racing’s momentum, Bloomberg Intelligence’s Mandeep Singh on Qualcomm’s Amazon chip deal, and Julie Macklowe on tariffs, whiskey and the rise of ready-made cocktails. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Evolution’s Compliance Checks Faulty, Unsealed Report Says
item.description: Evolution AB had “ineffective” compliance procedures for checking if its casino games were accessible in markets where gambling is illegal, according to a 2022 report made public in a Tuesday court filing.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon

item.title: X Probed by Irish Watchdog Over Age, Parental Control Concerns
item.description: Ireland’s media watchdog launched an investigation into X, over concerns the social media platform owned by Elon Musk breached age and parental control provisions.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Fletcher

item.title: UK to Make Apple, Google Block Nude Images on Kids’ Devices
item.description: The UK government will require technology companies such as Apple Inc. and Google to stop children from taking, sharing or viewing nude images on their phones and tablets, Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy told the House of Commons on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Reid

item.title: Qualcomm Lands Amazon as Customer for Push Into AI Chips
item.description: Qualcomm Inc. signed up Amazon.com Inc. as a data center chip customer and investor, scoring a major win in its bid to benefit from soaring artificial intelligence spending.
item.dc:creator: Ian King

item.title: Farmers Embrace AI More Than Any Other Tech, McKinsey Says
item.description: Artificial intelligence use is surging on farms as growers look for some high-tech help in planning and managing operations after years of scaling back on spending, according to McKinsey & Co.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hirtzer

item.title: Boston Scientific, Stryker Drop on Fallout From Cyber Attacks
item.description: Boston Scientific Corp. and Stryker Corp. shares fell after the medical device companies said they are dealing with the repercussions of separate cyber attacks that curtailed their ability to get products to customers and dented sales, with damage that could last for months.
item.dc:creator: Anna Edney
